name: The Fight
description: Drag, tension, the rod's angle, and how a fish gets away.

pages.title: The Fight
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- The **drag** gives line when a fish pulls harder than it: set it below what the line holds.
- **Hold use** to reel, **left-click** to lift; **]**, **[** or scroll: drag.
- Look **at the fish**: a bent rod soaks its runs and jumps.
- Keep the line tight, or the hook comes loose.

Once struck, the fish pulls. While it pulls less than the drag, holding use reels it in, slower the harder it pulls. When it pulls more, the drag slips and line runs out at the fish's speed.\
\
A fish tires against the line's tension, so a drag set too light never wears it out. A tired fish within 1.5 m is landed; a fresh one bolts again.\
\
Walking or sailing away pulls on the fish: a small one is towed along, a big one takes line through the drag.

**What the fish does.** It holds and pulls, swaying as it works and drifting round you; it **runs**, pulling harder and sweeping off to one side; it **shakes its head** (the line throbs); it **swims at you**, and the line goes slack unless you reel faster than it comes; tired, it **sulks** a moment, pulling less: gain line then.

**Stretch.** The line stretches and the rod bends, so the tension builds and eases rather than jumping. String and mono give a lot, which softens every lunge; braid hardly gives, so you feel everything at once. Slack line hangs in a curve from the tip.

**Lifting.** Hold attack (left click) to lift the rod; let go and it comes back down. It flicks up with a light fish and lifts slowly under a heavy one (the bar left of the tension bar).\
\
A lift draws the fish back by most of the rod's length (0.9 m of line per metre of rod), against the drag but not against the reel's crank.

**Pumping.** Reel while the rod comes down and it comes down as fast as the reel takes up the line, with no load on the crank. Lift, wind down, lift again: that brings in a fish too heavy to reel.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** let the rod down without reeling and the line goes slack; slack for over a second can throw the hook.

**Changing the drag.** Any time a rod is in hand: before casting, while waiting, mid-fight.

- the **Drag +** / **Drag -** keys, **]** and **[** (rebind them under Create Galore Fishing in Controls)
- the scroll wheel while a line is out, or while sneaking

The setting stays on the rod. A pole has no drag.

**The rod's angle.** The rod is held a little above where you look, and up to 60° higher while lifted. Look at the fish and the rod bends, soaking the spikes of runs and jumps. Look away or up and it also adds side pressure, which tires the fish faster.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** pointing the rod straight down the line soaks nothing. Every jump hits the line in full.

**The HUD** while a line is out:

- three upright stress bars at the right: **Line** against its test (tick where the drag slips), **Reel** against its drag and crank, **Rod** against its rating: green, yellow from 60%%, red from 85%%, the line blue when slack
- a thin bar by the rod's: how high it is lifted

**Above the hotbar:** the drag, the line out and the line left, and the alerts **Drag slipping**, **Slack line!**, **Swimming at you!**, **It's running!** (only while the fish takes line), **Head shakes!** and **It's sulking**.

**How a fish gets away** (chat says what broke and why):

- **Snapped line**: drag at or over the line's test (or the leader's). A drag below it slips first: the line holds.
- **Bitten off**: teeth fray non-steel line, faster the bigger the fish is for it; one far too big bites through at once.

- **Rod broke**: over its rating, or worn through.
- **Reel seized**: ground through.
- **Threw the hook**: slack line, a jump, or a hook too small.
- **Spooled**: every metre out.

A snapped, bitten, spooled or seized line loses the line that was out plus a few metres, with the leader, hook, float or lure and the one bait on the hook. Bait still waiting in the rod stays, and the line left is unfrayed. A rod that breaks gives its parts back.

**Wear.** Every fight wears the rod, reel, leader, hook and float, sinker or lure a little, even an easy catch: the rod and reel lose 1 durability, the small parts last about 200 fights. A line never wears from use or hard fights: it holds or snaps. Only teeth fray it. Tooltips show how worn or frayed a part is.

**Breaking.** A rod or reel worn through, or a line frayed through by teeth, breaks mid-fight and the fish is gone. A leader, hook, float, sinker or lure can wear out mid-fight too, but a hooked fish stays on. Check your tackle before going after a big one.
**Grinding.** Reeling while line runs out grinds the reel: after half a second it wears fast, with the square of the drag (half the reel's drag grinds a quarter as fast).

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** A rod loaded above 70%% of its rating wears; above its rating it can crack. A worn rod holds less (down to 60%% when nearly broken), a frayed line holds less (down to half its test; the rod's tooltip, the drag readout and the HUD show what it holds now), a worn reel's drag gets jerky.

Toothy fish include pike, muskellunge, gar, piranha, barracuda, sharks, morays, anglerfish, lionfish and the Dragon Fish. Without an iron or steel leader their teeth fray the line a little all fight and more on each run or jump, with the square of their pull against the line's test; one pulling over three times the test can bite through at once.

The fight has its own sounds: the drag ratchet clicks as line leaves the spool (a slow tick when a fish leans on it, a scream on a fast run), the reel cranks and grinds, the line creaks above about 65%% of its breaking load, and snaps with a twang.\
\
Leaving the rod's hand, logging out or the chunk unloading reels the line in: a fish on is lost.
